evidence_text: Eight genes belong to the acute phase response (APR) pro-inflammatory protein family, including Saa3,25 Timp1,26 Plscr1,27 Cxcl9,28 Cd14,29 Hamp,30 Hpx,31 and Serpina10.32 Notably, the most differentially expressed gene, Saa3, which is downregulated by a fold change of −18.40 (p = 1E−7) in the CD47-modified group, is a murine APR apolipoprotein gene produced in hepatic or extrahepatic tissues and responds to systemic pro-inflammatory stimulation.33,34 Other genes, including Gbp2,35 Gbp6,36 Bmper,37 and Id1,38 involved in phagocytosis, autophagy, and endocytosis, were also significantly downregulated in the CD47-modified group.

Peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) recruitment is an indicator of inflammatory stimuli.24 To test whether CD47-modified LNP-mRNA are less inflammatory than unmodified LNPs, we compared PBMC counts in mice treated with either unmodified LNP-mRNA or CD47/LNP-mRNA after i.v. These data indicate that CD47-modified LNP-mRNA are less inflammatory compared to unmodified LNP-mRNA. Our previous work showed that LNP-mRNA administration exaggerates pre-existing inflammation.16 To further test whether CD47-modified LNP-mRNA are less inflammatory than unmodified LNP-mRNA, we treated mice with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to induce an inflammatory state, followed by the administration of CD47/LNP-mRNA or unmodified LNP-mRNA; then, we assessed the level of pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 (IL-6) in the serum. at 2 mg/kg to induce systemic inflammation.
